questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in simple past tense.

A. Arun knew the concepts of geometry.

B. Arun had been knowing the concepts of geometry.

C. Arun had known the concepts of geometry.

D. Arun was knowing the concepts of geometry.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**Arun knew the concepts of geometry.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• We are required to select a sentence in simple past tense.
 
• The simple past is a verb tense that is used to talk about things that happened or existed before now.
 
• **Simple past tense is formed using the formula:**
 
 
• **Subject + past form of the verb(verb 2) + rest of the sentence.**
 
 
 
• **The verb "knew" is the simple past tense form of "know."**
 
• "Arun" is the subject of the sentence, and "the concepts of geometry" is the direct object.
 
• Therefore, the sentence in simple past tense is "Arun knew the concepts of geometry."

Hence, **the correct answer is option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 2, "Arun had been knowing the concepts of geometry," is in the past perfect continuous tense, which refers to an action that started in the past and continued up until another point in the past. However, this tense is not appropriate for this sentence.
 
• Option 3, "Arun had known the concepts of geometry," is in the past perfect tense, which refers to an action that was completed before another action in the past. This tense is grammatically correct, but the simple past tense is more appropriate in this case.
 
• Option 4, "Arun was knowing the concepts of geometry," is in the past continuous tense, which refers to an action that was in progress at a specific time in the past. However, this tense is not appropriate for this sentence.
